relationship: parallel union of justice and devotion
rationale: Love of righteousness and sincere seeking of the Lord correspond to Micah's requirement to do justice and walk with God.
source_text: Love righteousness, you who judge the earth; think of the Lord in goodness, and seek Him in simplicity of heart.

target_units.text: Has it been declared to you, O man, what is good? Or what does the Lord seek from you, except to do justice, and to love mercy, and to be ready to walk with the Lord your God?

relationship: parallel rejection of testing God
rationale: Wisdom connects finding God with refusing to test Him; Deuteronomy expressly forbids putting the Lord to the test.
source_text: For He is found by those who do not put Him to the test, and He makes Himself known to those who do not distrust Him.

target_units.text: You shall not put the Lord your God to the test, as you tested Him at Testing.

relationship: parallel moral separation from God
rationale: Crooked reasoning separates people from God here, while Isaiah describes offenses standing between the people and God.
source_text: For crooked reasonings separate from God, and power, when put to the test, exposes the foolish.

target_units.text: Instead, your offenses stand between you and God, and because of your sins He has turned His face away from you so as not to show mercy.

relationship: internal parallel of wisdom's purity
rationale: Wisdom's refusal to inhabit an evil-devising soul corresponds to the later declaration that nothing defiled enters her pure outflow.
source_text: For wisdom will not enter a soul that devises evil, nor will she dwell in a body indebted to sin.

target_units.text: For she is a breath of God’s power and a pure outflow of the Almighty’s glory; therefore nothing defiled enters into her.

relationship: related wrongdoing against the holy Spirit
rationale: The spirit of discipline flees deceit and is put to shame when injustice comes upon it; Ephesians likewise places its warning against grieving the Holy Spirit beside the removal of malice and slander.
source_text: For a holy spirit of discipline will flee deceit and depart from senseless reasonings, and will be put to shame when injustice comes upon it.

target_units.text: And do not grieve the Holy Spirit of God, in whom you were sealed for the day of redemption.
Let all bitterness and rage and anger and shouting and slander be taken away from you, with all malice.

relationship: close heart-and-kidneys examination motif
rationale: Both passages portray God examining the heart and kidneys, grounding accountability in knowledge of a person's interior life.
source_text: For wisdom is a spirit that loves humanity, and she will not acquit a blasphemer of what his lips have said; for God is a witness of his kidneys, a true overseer of his heart, and a hearer of his tongue.

target_units.text: I, the Lord, examine hearts and test kidneys, to give each according to his ways and the fruits of his practices.

relationship: parallel universal presence of God's Spirit
rationale: The Spirit filling the inhabited world corresponds to the psalm's inability to escape God's Spirit in heaven, Hades or the distant sea.
source_text: For the Spirit of the Lord has filled the inhabited world, and that which holds all things together has knowledge of utterance.

target_units.text: Where can I go from Thy Spirit, and where can I flee from Thy face?
If I ascend to heaven, Thou art there; if I descend into Hades, Thou art present.
if I take up my wings at dawn and settle at the sea’s farthest reaches,
indeed, even there Thy hand will guide me, and Thy right hand will hold me fast.

relationship: parallel accountability for speech
rationale: Unjust speech cannot escape convicting justice; Matthew similarly makes spoken words subject to accounting and condemnation.
source_text: Therefore no one who speaks unjust things will escape notice, nor will convicting justice pass him by.

target_units.text: But I tell you that people will give account on the day of judgment for every idle word they speak.
For by your words you will be justified, and by your words you will be condemned.”

relationship: related divine knowledge of thought and speech
rationale: The examination of deliberations and report of words correspond to God's knowledge of the psalmist's reasonings and tongue.
source_text: For there will be an examination of the ungodly person’s deliberations, and the report of his words will come to the Lord to expose his lawless deeds.

target_units.text: Thou knewest my sitting and my rising; Thou didst understand my reasonings from afar.
Thou didst trace my path and my measuring cord, and Thou didst foresee all my ways.
For there is no word on my tongue,
behold, Lord, Thou knewest all things, the last and the first; Thou didst form me and place Thy hand upon me.

relationship: narrative example of heard grumbling
rationale: Wisdom says grumbling is not hidden; Numbers explicitly reports the Lord hearing the congregation's grumbling and their words in His ears.
source_text: For an ear of jealousy listens to all things, and the murmur of grumblings is not hidden.

target_units.text: How long with this evil congregation? They grumble before Me; I have heard the sons of Israel’s grumbling that they have directed against you.
Say to them, I live, says the Lord: I will certainly do to you just as you have spoken into My ears.

relationship: parallel restraint of harmful speech
rationale: Restraint of slander and destructive utterance corresponds to the prohibition of rotten speech and the removal of slander.
source_text: Therefore guard yourselves against useless grumbling, and restrain your tongue from slander; for a secret utterance will not pass away without effect, and a lying mouth destroys a soul.

target_units.text: Let no rotten word come out of your mouth, but only what is good for building up as needed, so that it may give grace to those who hear.
And do not grieve the Holy Spirit of God, in whom you were sealed for the day of redemption.
Let all bitterness and rage and anger and shouting and slander be taken away from you, with all malice.

relationship: parallel appeal to abandon death-bringing wrongdoing
rationale: Wisdom warns against drawing destruction through one's works; Ezekiel urges the people to cast away impieties and asks why they are dying.
source_text: Do not pursue death through the wandering of your life, nor draw destruction upon yourselves through the works of your hands;

target_units.text: I will judge you, each according to his way, house of Israel, says the Lord. Turn back and turn away from all your impieties, and they will not become a punishment of injustice for you.
Cast away from yourselves all your impieties with which you acted impiously against Me, and make yourselves a new heart and a new spirit. Why are you dying, house of Israel?

relationship: close denial of delight in death
rationale: God's lack of delight in the destruction of the living corresponds to His declaration that He does not desire the dying person's death.
source_text: For God did not make death, neither does He delight in the destruction of the living.

target_units.text: For I do not desire the death of the one who dies, says the Lord.”

relationship: related goodness and sustenance of creation
rationale: Wisdom calls created things life-preserving; Genesis describes plants given as food and judges the whole creation very good, without making Wisdom's additional claims about Hades.
source_text: For He created all things that they might exist, and the created things of the world are life-preserving; there is no poison of destruction in them, nor is Hades’ dominion upon the earth.

target_units.text: And God said, “Behold, I have given you every plant sowing seed upon all the earth, and every tree that bears fruit containing seed. These shall be yours for food.
And to every wild beast of the earth, every bird of heaven, and every creeping thing upon the earth that has life within it, I have given every green plant for food.” And it was so.
And God saw all that He had made, and behold, it was very good. And there was evening, and there was morning: a sixth day.

relationship: parallel association of righteousness with life
rationale: Wisdom's immortality of righteousness corresponds to life in the ways of righteousness, without treating the proverb as a full account of immortality.
source_text: For righteousness is immortal.

target_units.text: In ways of righteousness is life, but the ways of those who remember wrongs lead to death.

relationship: close covenant-with-death motif
rationale: The ungodly make a covenant with death here; Isaiah exposes rulers who claim agreements with death and a covenant with Hades.
source_text: But the ungodly summoned him by their hands and words; considering him a friend, they wasted away, and they made a covenant with him, because they are worthy to belong to his portion.

target_units.text: Because you said, “We made a covenant with Hades and agreements with death; if a rushing storm passes, it will certainly not come upon us. We made falsehood our hope and will be sheltered by deceit,”

relationship: related mortal lament within different arguments
rationale: The ungodly begin with short, sorrowful life and irreversible death; Job's lament describes short-lived humanity and the dead lying asleep until heaven is no longer stitched together. Wisdom subsequently rejects the ungodly conclusion.
source_text: For they said among themselves, reasoning wrongly: “Our life is short and sorrowful, and there is no healing when a human being dies, and no one has been known to return from Hades.

target_units.text: “For a mortal born of woman is short-lived and full of wrath.
Like a flower that blossomed, he fell away; he fled like a shadow and will not remain.
Didst Thou not take account of this one also, and bring him into judgment before Thee?
For who will be clean from filth? No one.
Even if his life on earth is one day, his months are numbered with Thee; Thou didst set a time, and he will certainly not go beyond it.
Leave him alone so that he may be quiet and take pleasure in life like a hired worker.
For a tree has hope: if it is cut down, it will blossom again, and its shoot will not fail.
For even if its root grows old in earth and its trunk dies in rock,
from the scent of water it will blossom and produce a harvest like a newly planted tree.
But a man who has died is gone; a mortal who has fallen is no more.
For in time a sea diminishes, and a river, left desolate, dries up.
But a person who lies down will certainly not rise until heaven is no longer stitched together; they will not wake from their sleep.

relationship: contrast concerning the human spirit's origin and end
rationale: The ungodly attribute existence to chance and reduce breath to smoke; Ecclesiastes instead describes the spirit as given by God and returning to Him.
source_text: For we came into being by chance, and afterward we will be as though we had not existed; for the breath in our nostrils is smoke, and reason is a spark in the movement of our heart;

target_units.text: and the dust returns to the earth as it was, and the spirit returns to God who gave it.

relationship: contrast concerning the spirit after death
rationale: The ungodly predict dispersion into air, whereas Ecclesiastes says the spirit returns to God; the relation is a contrast, not agreement with the quoted speakers.
source_text: when it is extinguished, the body will become ashes, and the spirit will disperse like insubstantial air.

target_units.text: and the dust returns to the earth as it was, and the spirit returns to God who gave it.

relationship: shared disappearing-cloud and lost-place imagery
rationale: The ungodly compare forgotten life to a vanishing cloud; Job likewise compares the dead to a cleared-away cloud whose former place no longer recognizes him.
source_text: And our name will be forgotten in time, and no one will remember our works; our life will pass like the traces of a cloud, and will disperse like mist, driven away by the sun’s rays and weighed down by its heat.

target_units.text: like a cloud cleared away from heaven. For if a person goes down to Hades, he will never come up again,
nor will he ever return again to his own house, nor will his place recognize him any longer.

relationship: shared shadow and bounded-life imagery
rationale: The quoted speakers describe a passing shadow and sealed allotted time; Job similarly depicts a fleeing shadow and a divinely fixed limit to life.
source_text: For our allotted time is the passing of a shadow, and there is no turning back from our end, because it has been sealed, and no one returns.

target_units.text: Like a flower that blossomed, he fell away; he fled like a shadow and will not remain.
Didst Thou not take account of this one also, and bring him into judgment before Thee?
For who will be clean from filth? No one.
Even if his life on earth is one day, his months are numbered with Thee; Thou didst set a time, and he will certainly not go beyond it.

relationship: parallel condemned response to mortality
rationale: The ungodly urge present enjoyment after denying hope beyond death; Isaiah condemns the feast justified by the claim that tomorrow brings death.
source_text: Come, then, and let us enjoy the good things that exist, and eagerly make use of creation as in youth.

target_units.text: but they made gladness and exultation, slaughtering calves and sacrificing sheep to eat meat and drink wine, saying, “Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die!”

relationship: parallel indulgence in wine
rationale: The ungodly resolve to fill themselves with costly wine; Isaiah condemns prolonged wine drinking that neglects the Lord's works.
source_text: Let us fill ourselves with costly wine and perfumes, and let no spring blossom pass us by.

target_units.text: Woe to those rising in the morning and pursuing strong drink, lingering into the evening, for wine will burn them up!
For with lyre and harp, drums and flutes they drink wine, but they do not look at the Lord’s works or consider the works of His hands.

relationship: parallel revelry claimed under approaching death
rationale: The speakers claim revelry as their portion in the argument begun with death; Isaiah's condemned revelers likewise make enjoyment their answer to impending death.
source_text: Let none of us be without a share in our revelry; let us leave tokens of our enjoyment everywhere, for this is our portion, and this our lot.

target_units.text: but they made gladness and exultation, slaughtering calves and sacrificing sheep to eat meat and drink wine, saying, “Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die!”

relationship: direct moral contrast over vulnerable people
rationale: The ungodly propose oppressing the poor and sparing no widow; Exodus forbids mistreating widows and pressing poor debtors.
source_text: Let us oppress the poor righteous person; let us not spare a widow, nor show regard for an old man’s many years of gray hair.

target_units.text: You shall not mistreat any widow or orphan.
But if you afflict them, and they cry aloud to Me, I will surely listen to their voice,
I will be angry with wrath and kill you with the sword. Your wives will become widows and your children orphans.
And if you lend silver to your poor brother beside you, you shall not press him hard, neither shall you lay interest upon him.

relationship: contrast between might and righteous judgment
rationale: The speakers make strength their law and dismiss weakness; the psalm requires judges to vindicate and rescue the poor and needy instead.
source_text: Let our strength be the law of righteousness, for what is weak is shown to be useless.

target_units.text: “How long do you judge injustice and favor sinners? Diapsalma.
Judge for the fatherless and the poor; vindicate the lowly and the needy.
Deliver the needy and the poor; rescue them from the hand of a sinner.”

relationship: parallel persecution of the righteous
rationale: The ungodly plot against the righteous critic; the psalm similarly describes sinners watching the righteous and drawing weapons against the upright.
source_text: Let us lie in wait for the righteous person, because he is troublesome to us and opposes our works; he reproaches us for sins against law and charges us with sins against our upbringing.

target_units.text: The sinner will watch the righteous closely and gnash his teeth at him.
But the Lord will laugh him to scorn, for He foresees that his day will come.
The sinners drew a sword and stretched their bow, to cast down the poor and needy, to slaughter the upright in heart.

relationship: related claim of divine parentage under hostility
rationale: The righteous person calls himself the Lord's child; John records Jesus calling God His Father amid murderous opposition. This is a thematic parallel, not an asserted identification of the speakers.
source_text: He professes to have knowledge of God and calls himself a child of the Lord.

target_units.text: But Jesus answered them, “My Father is working even now, and I am working.”
For this reason, therefore, the Jews sought all the more to kill Him, because He not only broke the Sabbath, but also called God His own Father, making Himself equal to God.

relationship: parallel hatred of a moral reprover
rationale: The righteous person's presence reproaches the plotters' thoughts; Amos describes hatred of one who reproves at the gates.
source_text: He has become a reproach to our thoughts; even the sight of him weighs upon us,

target_units.text: They hated one who reproved at the gates and abhorred a holy word.

relationship: parallel separation of a righteous way of life
rationale: The righteous person's different paths correspond to the blessed person's refusal to walk in ungodly counsel and devotion to the Lord's law.
source_text: because his life is unlike that of others, and his paths are different.

target_units.text: Blessed is the man who did not walk in the counsel of the ungodly, and did not stand in the way of sinners, and did not sit in the seat of pestilent men;
but his will is in the Lord’s law, and on His law he will meditate day and night.

relationship: shared separation and divine-fatherhood motifs
rationale: Keeping away from impurities and calling God father correspond to the instruction to separate from uncleanness and the promise of God as Father.
source_text: He has reckoned us counterfeit, and keeps away from our ways as from impurities; he calls the final lot of the righteous blessed, and boasts that God is his father.

target_units.text: Therefore come out from their midst and be separated, says the Lord, and do not touch anything unclean; and I will receive you.
And I will be a Father to you, and you will be sons and daughters to Me, says the Lord Almighty.”

relationship: parallel hostile test of a righteous person's claims
rationale: The plotters propose testing whether his words prove true; the mockers demand rescue as a test of belief in Jesus and His trust in God.
source_text: Let us see whether his words are true, and test what will happen at his departure.

target_units.text: “He saved others; Himself He cannot save. He is King of Israel! Let Him come down from the cross now, and we will believe in Him.
He trusts in God; let Him rescue Him now, if He desires Him, for He said, ‘I am God’s Son.’”

relationship: close sonship-and-rescue taunt
rationale: Both hostile speeches connect claimed divine sonship with the demand that God rescue the persecuted person.
source_text: For if the righteous person is a son of God, He will help him and rescue him from the hand of his opponents.

target_units.text: He trusts in God; let Him rescue Him now, if He desires Him, for He said, ‘I am God’s Son.’”

relationship: related abusive testing of the persecuted
rationale: The proposed examination through insult and torture corresponds to the soldiers' mocking, spitting and striking of Jesus before crucifixion.
source_text: Let us examine him with insult and torture, so that we may know his gentleness and test his endurance of wrong.

target_units.text: Then the governor’s soldiers took Jesus into the praetorium and gathered the whole cohort around Him.
They stripped Him and put a scarlet cloak around Him.
They wove a crown from thorns, placed it upon His head, and put a reed in His right hand. Kneeling before Him, they mocked Him, saying, “Greetings, King of the Jews!”
They spat on Him, took the reed, and kept striking Him upon the head.
After mocking Him, they stripped off the cloak, dressed Him in His own garments, and led Him away to crucify Him.

relationship: related shameful execution and expected divine care
rationale: The ungodly condemn a person whose claim of divine care they challenge; Matthew places the same rescue challenge around the crucified Jesus.
source_text: Let us condemn him to a shameful death, for, according to his words, he will be visited with care.”

target_units.text: Those passing by reviled Him, shaking their heads
and saying, “Thou who destroyest the sanctuary and buildest it in three days, save Thyself! If Thou art God’s Son, come down from the cross.”
Likewise the chief priests, mocking with the scribes and elders, said,
“He saved others; Himself He cannot save. He is King of Israel! Let Him come down from the cross now, and we will believe in Him.
He trusts in God; let Him rescue Him now, if He desires Him, for He said, ‘I am God’s Son.’”

relationship: parallel moral blindness of understanding
rationale: Wickedness blinds the plotters here; Ephesians links darkened understanding and ignorance to hardness of heart and impure conduct.
source_text: They reasoned these things and went astray, for their wickedness blinded them;

target_units.text: So I say this and testify in the Lord: you must no longer walk as the Gentiles also walk, in the futility of their mind,
being darkened in understanding, alienated from the life of God because of the ignorance in them, because of the hardness of their heart.
Having become unfeeling, they handed themselves over to licentiousness for the practice of every impurity in greed.

relationship: internal contrast of denied and promised reward
rationale: The ungodly fail to recognize holiness's reward; the following account explicitly promises immortality, benefits and mercy to the faithful.
source_text: they did not know the mysteries of God, nor hope for a reward of holiness, nor recognize a prize for blameless souls.

target_units.text: For even if they are punished in the sight of human beings, their hope is full of immortality;
and after being disciplined a little, they will receive great benefits, because God tested them and found them worthy of Himself.
Like gold in a crucible He tested them, and like a sacrificial whole burnt offering He accepted them.
And at the time of their visitation they will shine out, and like sparks among stubble they will dart about.
They will judge nations and rule over peoples, and the Lord will reign over them unto the ages.
Those who trust in Him will understand truth, and the faithful will remain with Him in love, for grace and mercy are for His chosen ones.

relationship: creation-image parallel
rationale: Wisdom's claim that humanity is God's image recalls Genesis's creation in God's image; Wisdom adds its explicit interpretation in terms of eternity and incorruption.
source_text: For God created the human being for incorruption and made him an image of His own eternity;

target_units.text: And God made man; in the image of God He made him; male and female He made them.

relationship: related deception-and-death narrative
rationale: Wisdom interprets death's entry through the devil's envy; Genesis supplies the serpent's deception and humanity's return to earth, without itself naming envy or the devil.
source_text: but through the devil’s envy death entered the world, and those who belong to his portion experience it.

target_units.text: And the Lord God said to the woman, “What is this you have done?” And the woman said, “The serpent deceived me, and I ate.”

And the Lord God said to the serpent: Because you have done this, cursed are you above all cattle and all the wild beasts of the earth. Upon your breast and belly you shall go, and earth you shall eat all the days of your life.
And I will put enmity between you and the woman, and between your seed and her seed. He shall watch for your head, and you shall watch for his heel.
And to the woman He said: I will greatly multiply your sorrows and your groaning; in sorrow you shall bear children. You shall turn toward your husband, and he shall rule over you.

And to Adam He said: Because you listened to the voice of your wife and ate from the tree of which alone I commanded you not to eat, cursed is the earth in your labours; in pain you shall eat of it all the days of your life.
Thorns and thistles it shall bring forth for you, and you shall eat the plants of the field.
By the sweat of your face you shall eat your bread, until you return to the earth from which you were taken; for earth you are, and unto earth you shall return.

relationship: shared divine-hand security and life
rationale: The righteous souls are secure in God's hand; Jesus likewise promises life and declares that no one can snatch His people from His or the Father's hand.
source_text: But the souls of the righteous are in the hand of God, and torment will surely not touch them.

target_units.text: And I give them eternal life, and they will certainly never perish, and no one will snatch them from My hand.
What My Father has given Me is greater than all, and no one can snatch from the Father’s hand.

relationship: parallel misunderstood death of the righteous
rationale: Foolish observers misread the righteous person's departure; Isaiah likewise says no one understands the removal of the righteous.
source_text: In the eyes of the foolish they seemed to have died, and their departure was reckoned a calamity,

target_units.text: See how the righteous man perished, and no one considers it in his heart. Righteous men are removed, and no one understands. For the righteous man was taken from the presence of injustice.

relationship: close righteous-death and peace parallel
rationale: Wisdom contrasts apparent destruction with peace; Isaiah describes the righteous person's burial in peace.
source_text: and their going away from us a destruction; but they are in peace.

target_units.text: His burial will be in peace; he has been removed from the midst.

relationship: related hope of immortality beyond mortality
rationale: The righteous hope in immortality despite apparent punishment; Paul likewise anticipates mortality putting on immortality and death's defeat.
source_text: For even if they are punished in the sight of human beings, their hope is full of immortality;

target_units.text: For this corruptible must put on incorruption, and this mortal must put on immortality.
But when this corruptible puts on incorruption and this mortal puts on immortality, then the written saying will come to pass: “Death has been swallowed up in victory.”

relationship: parallel beneficial divine discipline
rationale: A little discipline brings great benefits here; Hebrews describes God's discipline as beneficial and producing righteousness afterward.
source_text: and after being disciplined a little, they will receive great benefits, because God tested them and found them worthy of Himself.

target_units.text: For they disciplined us for a few days according to what seemed right to them, but He for our benefit, so that we may share in His holiness.
Now every discipline seems for the present to be a matter of sorrow, not joy, but afterward it yields the peaceful fruit of righteousness to those trained through it.

relationship: close gold-furnace and divine-testing image
rationale: Wisdom likens God's testing to gold in a crucible; Proverbs similarly compares the testing of gold and silver to hearts chosen before the Lord.
source_text: Like gold in a crucible He tested them, and like a sacrificial whole burnt offering He accepted them.

target_units.text: As silver and gold are tested in a furnace, so hearts are chosen before the Lord.

relationship: parallel future radiance of the faithful
rationale: The righteous shine at their visitation; Daniel likewise depicts the understanding and faithful as heavenly lights and stars.
source_text: And at the time of their visitation they will shine out, and like sparks among stubble they will dart about.

target_units.text: Those who understand will appear like heaven’s lights, and those who strengthen my words like the stars of heaven for the age of the age.

relationship: parallel judgment and kingdom of the holy ones
rationale: Wisdom promises the righteous judgment over nations under the Lord's reign; Daniel assigns judgment and everlasting kingship to the holy people.
source_text: They will judge nations and rule over peoples, and the Lord will reign over them unto the ages.

target_units.text: until the Ancient of Days came and gave judgment to the holy ones of the Most High. The time was given, and the holy ones took possession of the kingship.
I was told concerning the fourth beast that a fourth kingdom would be upon the earth, surpassing the whole earth, overturning it and grinding it down.
As for the kingdom’s ten horns, ten kings will arise, and another king will arise after them. He will surpass the earlier ones in evils and humble three kings.
He will speak words against the Most High, wear down the holy ones of the Most High, and expect to alter seasons and law. Everything will be handed into his hands for a time, times, and half a time.
The judgment will sit; they will destroy the authority and plan to defile and destroy completely.

He gave the kingdom, authority, their greatness, and rule over all the kingdoms under heaven to a holy people of the Most High, to reign with everlasting kingship; all authorities will be subject to him and obey him.

relationship: parallel remaining in divine love
rationale: The faithful remain with God in love here; Jesus similarly calls His disciples to remain in His love through keeping His commandments.
source_text: Those who trust in Him will understand truth, and the faithful will remain with Him in love, for grace and mercy are for His chosen ones.

target_units.text: Just as the Father loved Me, I also loved you. Remain in My love.
If you keep My commandments, you will remain in My love, just as I have kept My Father’s commandments and remain in His love.

relationship: parallel judgment according to unrighteous conduct
rationale: Wisdom connects punishment to ungodly reasoning and departure from righteousness; Romans contrasts reward for good with wrath upon those obeying injustice.
source_text: But the ungodly will have punishment in keeping with their reasoning— those who neglected what is righteous and departed from the Lord.

target_units.text: But by your hardness and unrepentant heart, you store up wrath for yourself on the day of wrath and revelation of God’s righteous judgment,
who will repay each according to his works:
to those who, through perseverance in good work, seek glory and honor and incorruptibility, eternal life;
but to those acting from selfish ambition, who disobey the truth but obey unrighteousness, wrath and fury,
affliction and distress upon every human soul that does evil—the Jew first and also the Greek;

relationship: close rejection of wisdom and discipline
rationale: Wisdom calls the despiser of wisdom and discipline wretched; Proverbs identifies despising both as the behavior of the ungodly.
source_text: For the one who despises wisdom and discipline is wretched; their hope is empty, their labors unprofitable, and their works useless.

target_units.text: The fear of God is the beginning of wisdom, and good understanding belongs to all who practice it. Reverence toward God is the beginning of perception, but the ungodly will despise wisdom and discipline.

relationship: related reversal of barrenness
rationale: Wisdom promises fruit to the undefiled barren woman; Isaiah tells a barren woman to rejoice in abundant children, using the image for a restored community rather than an identical individual situation.
source_text: For blessed is the undefiled barren woman, who has not known a bed of transgression; she will have fruit at the visitation of souls,

target_units.text: “Rejoice, barren woman who does not give birth! Break out and cry aloud, you who do not labor in childbirth, because the deserted woman’s children are more numerous than those of the woman who has a husband,” for the Lord has spoken.

relationship: close faithful-eunuch and temple-inheritance parallel
rationale: Both promise faithful eunuchs an honored portion in God's house; Isaiah expressly adds an everlasting name better than sons and daughters.
source_text: and the eunuch who has done no lawless deed with his hand and has not conceived evil against the Lord; for a choice favor will be given him for his faithfulness, and a more delightful portion in the Lord’s temple.

target_units.text: Thus says the Lord: “To the eunuchs who keep My Sabbaths, choose what I wish, and hold fast to My covenant,
I will give them in My house and wall a renowned place better than sons and daughters; I will give them an everlasting name, and it will not fail.

relationship: parallel righteous fruit as life
rationale: The glorious fruit of good labor and unfailing root of understanding correspond to a tree of life growing from righteousness's fruit.
source_text: For the fruit of good labors is glorious, and the root of understanding does not fail.

target_units.text: From the fruit of righteousness a tree of life grows, but the lives of lawless people are taken away before their time.

relationship: internal development of unfruitful unlawful offspring
rationale: The failure of offspring from an unlawful bed is developed in the following chapter's illegitimate shoots and useless fruit.
source_text: But the children of adulterers will not reach fulfillment, and offspring from an unlawful bed will disappear.

target_units.text: But the prolific multitude of the ungodly will be of no use; from illegitimate shoots it will not send a root deep down, nor establish a secure foundation.
For even if it flourishes in branches for a time, standing insecurely, it will be shaken by wind and uprooted by the force of winds.
Unfulfilled branches will be broken off, and their fruit will be useless, unripe for eating, and fit for nothing.

relationship: internal contrast between age and moral honor
rationale: Long life does not secure honor for the offspring described here; the next chapter explains honorable age through understanding and an unstained life rather than years.
source_text: For even if they become long-lived, they will be reckoned as nothing, and their old age will be without honor at the end;

target_units.text: For honorable old age is not length of time, nor is it measured by a number of years;
rather, understanding is gray hair for human beings, and an unstained life is the maturity of old age.

relationship: explicit same-chapter contrast of hope after death
rationale: The offspring described here have no hope if they die quickly, in contrast to the righteous whose hope is full of immortality despite their apparent affliction.
source_text: and if they die quickly, they will have no hope, nor consolation on the day of decision.

target_units.text: For even if they are punished in the sight of human beings, their hope is full of immortality;

relationship: internal elaboration of the unrighteous end
rationale: The harsh end of an unrighteous generation is elaborated as dishonor, anguish, lost remembrance and a reckoning of sins.
source_text: For the ends of an unrighteous generation are harsh.

target_units.text: And afterward they will become a dishonored corpse and an object of outrage among the dead for ever; for He will dash them down headlong, speechless, and shake them from their foundations; they will be laid utterly waste, and will be in anguish, and their remembrance will perish.
They will come in dread at the reckoning of their sins, and their lawless deeds will confront and convict them.

relationship: parallel enduring honor beyond children
rationale: Wisdom values childlessness with virtue through immortal remembrance; Isaiah promises faithful eunuchs an everlasting name better than sons and daughters.
source_text: Childlessness with virtue is better, for immortality is in its remembrance, because it is recognized both by God and by human beings.

target_units.text: I will give them in My house and wall a renowned place better than sons and daughters; I will give them an everlasting name, and it will not fail.

relationship: shared contest and enduring-crown imagery
rationale: Virtue is pictured winning undefiled prizes and marching crowned; Paul likewise uses disciplined athletic competition for an incorruptible crown.
source_text: When it is present, people imitate it, and when it has departed, they long for it; throughout the age it marches crowned in triumph, having won the contest for undefiled prizes.

target_units.text: Do you not know that all the runners in a stadium run, but one receives the prize? Run in such a way that you may obtain it.
Everyone who competes exercises self-control in all things. They do so to receive a perishable wreath, but we an imperishable one.

relationship: contrast of rooted righteous life and unstable ungodliness
rationale: Wisdom denies the ungodly a deep root; the psalm contrasts the righteous tree beside water with ungodly chaff carried away.
source_text: But the prolific multitude of the ungodly will be of no use; from illegitimate shoots it will not send a root deep down, nor establish a secure foundation.

target_units.text: He will be like the tree planted beside the outlets of waters, which will give its fruit in its season, and whose leaf will not fall off; and everything he does will be prospered.
Not so the ungodly, not so, but like chaff which the wind flings away from the face of the earth.

relationship: shared wind-driven instability of ungodliness
rationale: The insecure branches are uprooted by winds; the psalm similarly depicts ungodly people as chaff driven away by wind, with a different plant image.
source_text: For even if it flourishes in branches for a time, standing insecurely, it will be shaken by wind and uprooted by the force of winds.

target_units.text: Not so the ungodly, not so, but like chaff which the wind flings away from the face of the earth.

relationship: parallel removal of fruitless growth
rationale: Wisdom's useless, broken branches correspond to the tree without good fruit being cut down; both use failed fruit to depict moral failure.
source_text: Unfulfilled branches will be broken off, and their fruit will be useless, unripe for eating, and fit for nothing.

target_units.text: Every tree that does not bear good fruit is cut down and thrown into fire.

relationship: parallel righteous death as peaceful removal
rationale: Wisdom grants rest to the righteous who die early; Isaiah presents the righteous person's removal from injustice and burial in peace.
source_text: But if a righteous person dies early, he will be at rest.

target_units.text: See how the righteous man perished, and no one considers it in his heart. Righteous men are removed, and no one understands. For the righteous man was taken from the presence of injustice.
His burial will be in peace; he has been removed from the midst.

relationship: parallel denial that years guarantee worth
rationale: Wisdom denies that honorable age is measured by years; Elihu similarly denies that the long-lived necessarily possess wisdom or judgment.
source_text: For honorable old age is not length of time, nor is it measured by a number of years;

target_units.text: I said, ‘Time is what speaks, and in many years people know wisdom.’
But there is a spirit in mortals, and the Almighty’s breath is what teaches.
The long-lived are not wise, nor do elders know judgment.

relationship: parallel wisdom rather than years as maturity
rationale: Wisdom substitutes understanding and an unstained life for gray hair; Elihu locates instruction in God's breath rather than mere length of life.
source_text: rather, understanding is gray hair for human beings, and an unstained life is the maturity of old age.

target_units.text: But there is a spirit in mortals, and the Almighty’s breath is what teaches.
The long-lived are not wise, nor do elders know judgment.

relationship: close pleasing-God and transfer motif
rationale: The unnamed righteous person pleases God and is transferred, closely recalling Enoch's pleasing God and being transferred; the Wisdom verse itself does not name Enoch.
source_text: Having become pleasing to God, he was loved, and while living among sinners he was transferred.

target_units.text: And Enoch pleased God, and was not found, for God transferred him.

relationship: parallel removal from surrounding evil
rationale: Wisdom describes removal lest evil alter the righteous mind; Isaiah says the righteous man is taken from the presence of injustice.
source_text: He was snatched away, lest evil change his understanding or deceit mislead his soul;

target_units.text: See how the righteous man perished, and no one considers it in his heart. Righteous men are removed, and no one understands. For the righteous man was taken from the presence of injustice.

relationship: parallel corrupting action of desire
rationale: Desire alters an innocent mind here; James describes desire enticing a person and giving birth to sin and death.
source_text: for the fascination of wickedness obscures what is good, and the wandering of desire alters an innocent mind.

target_units.text: But each person is tempted when drawn away and enticed by his own desire.
Then desire, after conceiving, gives birth to sin; and sin, when fully grown, gives birth to death.

relationship: explicit same-chapter explanation of mature short life
rationale: A short life can fulfill long years because the earlier lines define honorable maturity by understanding and an unstained life rather than elapsed time.
source_text: Having been brought to completion in a short time, he fulfilled long years;

target_units.text: For honorable old age is not length of time, nor is it measured by a number of years;
rather, understanding is gray hair for human beings, and an unstained life is the maturity of old age.

relationship: close misunderstood removal of the righteous
rationale: Both describe the righteous person's removal from wickedness and observers who fail to understand or take it to heart.
source_text: for his soul was pleasing to the Lord; therefore he hastened from the midst of wickedness. Yet the peoples saw and did not understand, nor set such a thing in their minds:

target_units.text: See how the righteous man perished, and no one considers it in his heart. Righteous men are removed, and no one understands. For the righteous man was taken from the presence of injustice.

relationship: internal recurrence of mercy for the chosen
rationale: This statement repeats the earlier assurance that grace and mercy belong to God's chosen, explaining the apparent loss of the righteous.
source_text: that grace and mercy are among His chosen ones, and visitation among His holy ones.

target_units.text: Those who trust in Him will understand truth, and the faithful will remain with Him in love, for grace and mercy are for His chosen ones.

relationship: related exemplary condemnation at judgment
rationale: The righteous dead expose the living ungodly here; Matthew similarly presents earlier repentant or wisdom-seeking people rising to condemn a later generation.
source_text: But a righteous person who has died will condemn the living ungodly, and youth brought swiftly to completion will condemn the many years of an unrighteous person’s old age.

target_units.text: Men of Nineveh will rise at the judgment with this generation and condemn it, because they repented at Jonah’s proclamation; and behold, something greater than Jonah is here.

The queen of the south will be raised at the judgment with this generation and condemn it, because she came from the ends of the earth to hear Solomon’s wisdom; and behold, something greater than Solomon is here.

relationship: parallel failure to understand a righteous person's end
rationale: Wisdom's observers do not understand God's purpose in the wise person's end; Isaiah likewise stresses the uncomprehended removal of the righteous.
source_text: For they will see a wise person’s end and will not understand what the Lord planned concerning him or for what purpose He kept him safe.

target_units.text: See how the righteous man perished, and no one considers it in his heart. Righteous men are removed, and no one understands. For the righteous man was taken from the presence of injustice.

relationship: close divine-laughter reversal
rationale: The Lord laughs at those who despise the righteous person's end; the psalm likewise portrays the Lord laughing at the sinner because his day is coming.
source_text: They will see and despise, but the Lord will laugh them to scorn.

target_units.text: But the Lord will laugh him to scorn, for He foresees that his day will come.

relationship: parallel destruction of the ungodly's remembrance
rationale: Wisdom joins the ungodly's destruction to vanished remembrance; the psalm likewise describes their erased name and destroyed memory.
source_text: And afterward they will become a dishonored corpse and an object of outrage among the dead for ever; for He will dash them down headlong, speechless, and shake them from their foundations; they will be laid utterly waste, and will be in anguish, and their remembrance will perish.

target_units.text: Thou didst rebuke nations, and the ungodly one perished; Thou didst erase their name for ever and for the age of the age.
The enemy’s swords failed utterly, and Thou didst pull down cities; their memory perished with a noise.

relationship: parallel reckoning of all deeds
rationale: Lawless deeds confront their authors at examination here; Ecclesiastes likewise places every deed, even what was overlooked, under divine judgment.
source_text: They will come in dread at the reckoning of their sins, and their lawless deeds will confront and convict them.

target_units.text: For God will bring every deed into judgment, concerning everything overlooked, whether good or evil.

relationship: parallel confidence of the righteous
rationale: The righteous person's bold stance before former tormentors corresponds to the proverb's righteous person being confident like a lion.
source_text: Then the righteous person will stand with great boldness before those who afflicted him and those who disregarded his labors.

target_units.text: An impious person flees when no one pursues, but a righteous person is confident like a lion.

relationship: related reversal of persecutors' expectations
rationale: Those who afflicted the righteous are astonished at his salvation; Isaiah likewise anticipates shame for those who hate the people addressed by the Lord.
source_text: When they see him, they will be troubled with terrible fear and astonished at his unexpected salvation.

target_units.text: Hear the Lord’s word, you who tremble at His word! Speak, our brothers, to those who hate us and loathe us, so that the Lord’s name may be glorified and seen in their rejoicing; and those people will be ashamed.

relationship: internal recognition of former error
rationale: The anguished repentance of the persecutors realizes the narrator's earlier verdict that their reasoning was astray and ignorant of God's reward.
source_text: They will speak among themselves in repentance, and in anguish of spirit they will groan and say:

target_units.text: They reasoned these things and went astray, for their wickedness blinded them;
they did not know the mysteries of God, nor hope for a reward of holiness, nor recognize a prize for blameless souls.

relationship: internal reversal of contempt and shame
rationale: The former mockers recall their insulting verdict on the righteous person's life and end, reversing the earlier proposal to torture him and condemn him to shameful death.
source_text: “This was the one whom we fools once made a laughingstock and a byword of reproach. We reckoned his life madness and his end dishonorable.

target_units.text: Let us examine him with insult and torture, so that we may know his gentleness and test his endurance of wrong.
Let us condemn him to a shameful death, for, according to his words, he will be visited with care.”

relationship: internal vindication of disputed divine sonship
rationale: The persecutors now recognize the righteous person's portion among God's sons and saints after previously treating his claim to divine sonship as something to disprove.
source_text: How was he counted among the sons of God, and how is his portion among the saints?

target_units.text: He professes to have knowledge of God and calls himself a child of the Lord.
He has become a reproach to our thoughts; even the sight of him weighs upon us,
because his life is unlike that of others, and his paths are different.
He has reckoned us counterfeit, and keeps away from our ways as from impurities; he calls the final lot of the righteous blessed, and boasts that God is his father.
Let us see whether his words are true, and test what will happen at his departure.
For if the righteous person is a son of God, He will help him and rescue him from the hand of his opponents.

relationship: parallel moral paths of light and darkness
rationale: The persecutors confess that righteousness's light did not shine upon their way; Proverbs contrasts the shining righteous path with the dark, stumbling way of the ungodly.
source_text: So we strayed from the way of truth, and the light of righteousness did not shine upon us, and the sun did not rise upon us.

target_units.text: But the ways of the righteous shine like light; they go forward and illuminate until the day comes right.
But the ways of the ungodly are dark; they do not know how they stumble.

relationship: parallel lawless paths opposed to the righteous way
rationale: Their admission of traveling destructive paths corresponds to the prohibition of ungodly ways and the contrast between righteous light and ungodly darkness.
source_text: We were filled with paths of lawlessness and destruction, and traveled through trackless deserts, but the way of the Lord we did not know.

target_units.text: Do not enter the ways of the ungodly or imitate the ways of the lawless.
Wherever they encamp, do not go there; turn away from them and pass by.
For they will not sleep unless they do harm; their sleep has been taken away, and they do not lie down.
For these people eat food of ungodliness and get drunk on lawless wine.
But the ways of the righteous shine like light; they go forward and illuminate until the day comes right.
But the ways of the ungodly are dark; they do not know how they stumble.

relationship: parallel exposure of wealth's inability to save
rationale: The persecutors question the benefit of boastful wealth; the rich fool's accumulated goods similarly fail to help when his life is demanded.
source_text: What did arrogance profit us? And what did wealth with boasting contribute to us?

target_units.text: And I will say to my soul, “Soul, you have many goods laid up for many years. Rest, eat, drink, be glad!”’
But God said to him, ‘Fool, this very night they demand your soul from you; and the things you have prepared—whose will they be?’
So it is with the one who stores up treasure for himself and is not rich toward God.”

relationship: shared fleeting-shadow image
rationale: The vanished advantages of the ungodly pass like a shadow; Bildad likewise calls human life on earth a shadow, within a different argument about limited knowledge.
source_text: All those things passed like a shadow and like a report rushing by;

target_units.text: For we are of yesterday and do not know; our life on earth is a shadow.

relationship: shared elusive path of a seagoing ship
rationale: Wisdom's ship leaves no discoverable wake; Proverbs names a seagoing ship's path among tracks the speaker cannot comprehend.
source_text: like a ship passing through surging water, whose trace cannot be found after it has crossed, nor the path of its keel among the waves;

target_units.text: the tracks of a flying eagle, and the ways of a snake upon a rock, and the paths of a seagoing ship, and the ways of a man in youth.

relationship: shared elusive aerial track
rationale: Wisdom describes a bird's vanished path through the air; Proverbs likewise names the tracks of a flying eagle among elusive things.
source_text: or like a bird that has flown through the air: no sign of its passage is found. It crossed the light air, lashed by the beat of its pinions and split by the force of its rushing wings; and afterward no sign of its passage was found in it;

target_units.text: the tracks of a flying eagle, and the ways of a snake upon a rock, and the paths of a seagoing ship, and the ways of a man in youth.

relationship: internal failure of the promised lasting mark
rationale: Those who planned to leave tokens of enjoyment everywhere now confess that they vanished without a sign of virtue; their proposed legacy is exposed as empty.
source_text: so we also were born and vanished, and had no sign of virtue to show, but were consumed in our wickedness.”

target_units.text: Let none of us be without a share in our revelry; let us leave tokens of our enjoyment everywhere, for this is our portion, and this our lot.

relationship: parallel wind-driven disappearance of ungodliness
rationale: The ungodly person's hope is wind-borne dust and dispersed smoke; the psalm similarly pictures the ungodly as chaff flung away by wind.
source_text: For the hope of an ungodly person is like dust borne by wind, and like fine frost driven by a storm; like smoke it was dispersed by wind, and like the memory of a guest who stayed one day it passed away.

target_units.text: Not so the ungodly, not so, but like chaff which the wind flings away from the face of the earth.

relationship: parallel enduring life under divine care
rationale: The righteous live forever under the Most High's care; Jesus likewise promises eternal life and security in His and the Father's hand.
source_text: But the righteous live for ever, and their reward is with the Lord, and the Most High takes care of them.

target_units.text: And I give them eternal life, and they will certainly never perish, and no one will snatch them from My hand.
What My Father has given Me is greater than all, and no one can snatch from the Father’s hand.

relationship: close royal-crown and divine-hand imagery
rationale: The righteous receive a crown and diadem from the Lord's hand; Isaiah calls restored Zion a crown of beauty and royal diadem in God's hand, with a different bearer of the image.
source_text: Therefore they will receive the royal crown of splendor and the diadem of beauty from the Lord’s hand, because with His right hand He will cover them and with His arm He will shield them.

target_units.text: You will be a crown of beauty in the Lord’s hand and a royal diadem in your God’s hand.

relationship: parallel divine-warrior imagery
rationale: God takes zeal as armor and turns creation against enemies; Isaiah likewise depicts God clothing Himself for righteous vengeance and coming in wrath.
source_text: He will take His zeal as full armor and make creation into weapons to repel His enemies;

target_units.text: He put on righteousness like a breastplate, placed a helmet of salvation on His head, and wrapped Himself in a garment of vengeance and the cloak,
as one who will repay recompense—reproach to His adversaries.
Those from the west will fear the Lord’s name, and those from sunrise the glorious name. For anger from the Lord will come like a violent river; it will come with wrath.

relationship: close breastplate-and-helmet imagery
rationale: Both clothe the divine warrior in righteousness as a breastplate and a helmet; Wisdom specifies unfeigned judgment, while Isaiah names salvation.
source_text: He will put on righteousness as a breastplate, and put on unfeigned judgment as a helmet;

target_units.text: He put on righteousness like a breastplate, placed a helmet of salvation on His head, and wrapped Himself in a garment of vengeance and the cloak,

relationship: related martial representation of divine wrath
rationale: Wisdom turns stern wrath into a sword; Isaiah portrays vengeance as divine clothing and the Lord's anger as a violent river. The shared theme is armed judgment, not identical weaponry.
source_text: and sharpen stern wrath into a sword; the world will fight together with Him against the senseless.

target_units.text: He put on righteousness like a breastplate, placed a helmet of salvation on His head, and wrapped Himself in a garment of vengeance and the cloak,
as one who will repay recompense—reproach to His adversaries.
Those from the west will fear the Lord’s name, and those from sunrise the glorious name. For anger from the Lord will come like a violent river; it will come with wrath.

relationship: close lightning-and-arrows imagery
rationale: Wisdom's aimed lightning bolts correspond to the Lord's arrows and multiplied lightning flashes scattering opponents in the psalm.
source_text: Well-aimed bolts of lightning will go forth, and from the clouds, as from a well-curved bow, they will leap at the target;

target_units.text: And the Lord thundered from heaven, and the Most High gave His voice.
And He sent out arrows and scattered them; He multiplied lightning flashes and threw them into turmoil.

relationship: narrative analogue for destructive divine hail
rationale: The hailstones hurled in fury recall the hail and fire that struck Egypt's people, livestock and vegetation; Exodus does not supply the catapult image.
source_text: and hailstones full of fury will be hurled from a catapult; the water of the sea will rage against them, and rivers will flood over them relentlessly.

target_units.text: Moses stretched out his hand toward heaven. The Lord sent thunder and hail, and fire ran over the earth. The Lord rained hail upon all the land of Egypt.
There was hail, with fire flaming amid the hail. The hail was very, very abundant, such as had never been in Egypt since a nation came to be there.
Throughout Egypt the hail struck people and livestock. It struck every plant in the plains and shattered all the trees there.

relationship: parallel storm sweeping away rulers
rationale: Wisdom joins storm-driven destruction to overturned rulers' thrones; Isaiah likewise depicts rulers deprived of power and carried away like brushwood by a storm.
source_text: A mighty wind will oppose them and winnow them away like a storm; lawlessness will lay the whole earth waste, and wrongdoing will overturn the thrones of rulers.

target_units.text: He gives rulers nothing to rule and made the earth as nothing.
For they will certainly not sow or plant, nor will their root take hold in the earth. He blew on them, and they dried; a storm will carry them away like brushwood.

relationship: close address to kings and judges
rationale: Both directly summon kings to understand and those who judge the earth to receive instruction.
source_text: Listen, then, kings, and understand; learn, judges of the ends of the earth.

target_units.text: And now, kings, understand; be instructed, all who judge the earth.

relationship: parallel instruction addressed to rulers
rationale: The rulers of multitudes are told to listen here; the psalm similarly tells kings to accept instruction and serve the Lord rather than face His anger.
source_text: Give ear, you who rule a multitude and boast over crowds of nations;

target_units.text: And now, kings, understand; be instructed, all who judge the earth.
Serve the Lord with fear, and exult in Him with trembling.
Take hold of instruction, lest the Lord become angry and you perish from a righteous way. When His fury burns quickly, blessed are all who have trusted in Him.

relationship: parallel divine source and service of authority
rationale: Wisdom locates rulers' authority in the Lord and subjects their conduct to examination; Romans likewise derives authority from God and calls it His servant for good.
source_text: for your rule was given you by the Lord, and your authority by the Most High, who will examine your works and search out your plans.

target_units.text: Let every soul submit to the higher authorities, for there is no authority except from God, and those that exist have been appointed by God.
Therefore the one who sets himself against authority has resisted God’s ordering, and those who resist will receive judgment upon themselves.
For rulers are not a terror to good work, but to evil. Do you want to be free from fear of the authority? Do the good, and you will have praise from it;

for it is God’s servant to you for good. But if you do evil, be afraid; for it does not bear the sword without purpose. For it is God’s servant, an avenger who brings wrath on the one who practices evil.

relationship: parallel rebuke of unjust judges
rationale: Wisdom indicts royal servants who judge wrongly; the psalm rebukes unjust judgment and demands protection of the poor and needy.
source_text: For though you were servants of His kingdom, you did not judge rightly, nor keep law, nor walk according to God’s purpose.

target_units.text: “How long do you judge injustice and favor sinners? Diapsalma.
Judge for the fatherless and the poor; vindicate the lowly and the needy.
Deliver the needy and the poor; rescue them from the hand of a sinner.”

relationship: parallel greater accountability for privilege
rationale: Wisdom warns that high position receives severe judgment; Luke's servant teaching likewise requires more from those entrusted with more.
source_text: He will come upon you terribly and swiftly, for a severe judgment falls upon those in high position.

target_units.text: That slave who knew his master’s will and did not prepare or act according to his will shall receive many blows.

But the one who did not know and did things deserving blows shall receive few. From everyone to whom much was given, much will be required; and from the one to whom they entrusted much, they will ask all the more.

relationship: parallel unequal severity of examination
rationale: The contrast between pardon for the least and powerful examination of the mighty corresponds to differing blows and responsibility in Luke, without equating rank with knowledge.
source_text: For the least is pardonable through mercy, but the powerful will be powerfully examined.

target_units.text: That slave who knew his master’s will and did not prepare or act according to his will shall receive many blows.

But the one who did not know and did things deserving blows shall receive few. From everyone to whom much was given, much will be required; and from the one to whom they entrusted much, they will ask all the more.

relationship: parallel divine impartiality
rationale: The Master refuses deference to greatness; Romans likewise states that there is no partiality with God.
source_text: For the Master of all will not shrink before anyone’s face or show deference to greatness, because He Himself made both small and great and provides for all alike;

target_units.text: For there is no partiality with God.

relationship: parallel accountability of those entrusted with much
rationale: The mighty face a forceful inquiry; Luke similarly says that those entrusted with much will be asked for more.
source_text: but a forceful inquiry awaits the mighty.

target_units.text: But the one who did not know and did things deserving blows shall receive few. From everyone to whom much was given, much will be required; and from the one to whom they entrusted much, they will ask all the more.

relationship: parallel wisdom's necessity for rulers
rationale: The call for rulers to learn wisdom corresponds to personified Wisdom's declaration that kings reign and rulers govern through her.
source_text: To you, therefore, rulers, my words are directed, so that you may learn wisdom and not fall away.

target_units.text: Through me kings reign, and rulers write righteousness.
Through me great men become great, and through me sovereigns rule the earth.

relationship: explicit same-chapter development of holy observance
rationale: The promise attached to holy observance and instruction is developed by the later link between keeping wisdom's laws and assurance of incorruption.
source_text: For those who keep holy things in holiness will be made holy, and those instructed in them will find a defense.

target_units.text: love is the keeping of her laws, and attention to laws is assurance of incorruption;

relationship: parallel desire for instructive words
rationale: The speaker urges longing for his words to gain instruction; Proverbs asks children to hear discipline and keep the teacher's utterance in their hearts.
source_text: Desire my words, then; long for them, and you will be instructed.

target_units.text: Listen, children, to a father’s discipline; pay attention to gain discernment,
for I give you a good gift; do not abandon my law.
For I too became a son obedient to a father and loved in a mother’s presence,
who used to speak to me and teach me: Let our word take hold in your heart;
keep commandments; do not forget or disregard an utterance of my mouth,

relationship: close love-seek-find wisdom promise
rationale: Both promise that people who love and seek wisdom will find her.
source_text: Wisdom is radiant and unfading; she is readily seen by those who love her and found by those who seek her.

target_units.text: I love those who love me, and those who seek me will find me.

relationship: parallel wisdom's initiative in making herself known
rationale: Wisdom goes ahead of those desiring her; Proverbs presents her publicly stationed at paths and gates, calling to humanity.
source_text: She goes ahead of those who desire her, making herself known first.

target_units.text: For she is on the high summits, and stands between the paths.
For she sits beside the gates of rulers, and is praised at the entrances:
“You, O human beings, I summon, and I send forth my voice to the children of humankind.

relationship: close vigilant-seeker and gate imagery
rationale: The early seeker finds wisdom beside his gates; Proverbs blesses the person who stays awake daily at her doors and entrances.
source_text: The one who rises early for her will not grow weary, for he will find her sitting beside his gates.

target_units.text: Happy is the man who will listen to me, and the person who will keep my ways, staying awake at my doors day by day, guarding the posts of my entrances.

relationship: parallel reflection bringing freedom from fear
rationale: Reflection and vigilance for wisdom release care; Proverbs similarly connects keeping counsel and thought with confident walking and peaceful sleep.
source_text: For to reflect upon her is the perfection of understanding, and the one who keeps watch for her will soon be free from care;

target_units.text: Son, do not drift away; keep my counsel and thought,
so that your soul may live and grace be around your neck.
There will be healing for your flesh and care for your bones,
so that you may walk all your ways confidently in peace, and your foot will certainly not stumble.
For if you sit, you will be fearless, and if you sleep, you will sleep pleasantly.

relationship: parallel wisdom meeting people on their paths
rationale: Wisdom seeks worthy people and appears on their paths; Proverbs likewise locates her between paths and at entrances, addressing human beings.
source_text: for she herself goes about seeking those worthy of her, appears graciously to them on their paths, and meets them in every thought.

target_units.text: For she is on the high summits, and stands between the paths.
For she sits beside the gates of rulers, and is praised at the entrances:
“You, O human beings, I summon, and I send forth my voice to the children of humankind.

relationship: related love and disciplined attachment to wisdom
rationale: Wisdom links desire for discipline with love; Proverbs joins loving wisdom to holding fast to discipline for one's life.
source_text: For her beginning is the truest desire for discipline, and concern for discipline is love;

target_units.text: and do not abandon her, and she will hold fast to you; love her, and she will keep you.
Fortify her, and she will exalt you; honor her so that she may embrace you,
so that she may give your head a crown of graces and shield you with a crown of delight.
Listen, son, and receive my words, and your years of life will multiply, so that many ways of living may be yours,
for I teach you ways of wisdom and lead you onto straight tracks.
For if you walk, your steps will not be shut in, and if you run, you will not grow weary.
Take hold of my discipline; do not release it, but keep it for yourself for your life.

relationship: parallel love expressed in commandment keeping
rationale: Wisdom defines love through keeping her laws; Jesus likewise connects love for Him with keeping His commandments, in a different personal setting.
source_text: love is the keeping of her laws, and attention to laws is assurance of incorruption;

target_units.text: “If you love Me, you will keep My commandments.

relationship: parallel wisdom leading to kingship
rationale: Wisdom says desire for her leads toward kingship; Proverbs states that kings reign through Wisdom.
source_text: Therefore desire for wisdom leads up to kingship.

target_units.text: Through me kings reign, and rulers write righteousness.

relationship: related moral establishment of a throne
rationale: Rulers are urged to honor wisdom to reign enduringly; Proverbs similarly connects the establishment of a ruling throne with righteousness.
source_text: If, then, you delight in thrones and scepters, rulers of peoples, honor wisdom, so that you may reign for ever.

target_units.text: One who does evil is an abomination to a king, for a throne of rule is prepared with righteousness.

relationship: parallel disclosure of wisdom's beginning
rationale: The promised account of wisdom from her origin corresponds to Proverbs' extended speech about Wisdom's beginning and presence at creation.
source_text: What wisdom is and how she came to be, I will declare, and I will not hide mysteries from you; instead I will trace her from the beginning of her origin, and bring the knowledge of her into the open, and I will certainly not pass truth by.

target_units.text: The Lord created me as the beginning of His ways, for His works.
Before the age He founded me, in the beginning,
before making the earth and before making the deeps, before the springs of the waters came forth,
before the mountains were established, and before all hills He gives me birth.
The Lord made countries and uninhabited places, and the inhabited extremities of the world beneath heaven.
When He was preparing heaven, I was present with Him, and when He was marking out His own throne upon winds.
When He was making the clouds above strong, and when He was setting the springs of the world beneath heaven secure,
and was making the foundations of the earth strong,
I was beside Him, fitting things together; I was the one in whom He delighted. Day by day I rejoiced before Him at every time,
when He rejoiced after completing the inhabited world, and delighted in the children of humankind.

relationship: parallel incompatibility of envy and true wisdom
rationale: The speaker refuses wasting envy because it has no share with wisdom; James likewise denies heavenly wisdom to bitter jealousy and contrasts it with pure, peaceable wisdom.
source_text: Nor will I travel with wasting envy, for it will have no share with wisdom.

target_units.text: But if you have bitter jealousy and selfish ambition in your heart, do not boast against the truth and lie against it.
This is not the wisdom coming down from above; it is earthly, merely natural, demonic.
For where there are jealousy and selfish ambition, there are disorder and every foul practice.
But the wisdom from above is first pure, then peaceable, considerate, open to persuasion, full of mercy and good fruits, impartial, without hypocrisy.

relationship: parallel communal safety through abundant counsel
rationale: The multitude of wise people safeguards the world here; Proverbs similarly locates deliverance in much counsel.
source_text: A multitude of wise people is the world’s salvation, and an understanding king is the stability of a people.

target_units.text: Those who have no steering fall like leaves, but deliverance is in much counsel.

relationship: parallel beneficial instruction
rationale: The appeal to be instructed for one's benefit corresponds to a father's good gift of discipline and law to attentive children.
source_text: Therefore be instructed by my words, and you will benefit.

target_units.text: Listen, children, to a father’s discipline; pay attention to gain discernment,
for I give you a good gift; do not abandon my law.

relationship: creation-from-earth background
rationale: The speaker traces his common mortality to the first earthborn man; Genesis narrates God's forming the human being from earth's dust.
source_text: I too am a mortal human being, equal to all, and a descendant of the first-formed earthborn man; in a mother’s womb I was sculpted into flesh,

target_units.text: And God formed man from the dust of the earth, and breathed into his face the breath of life; and man became a living soul.

relationship: narrative example of ordinary infant care
rationale: The royal speaker recalls swaddling and care; Luke likewise depicts the newborn Jesus wrapped in swaddling cloths, a shared concrete feature rather than proof of identical circumstances.
source_text: I was brought up in swaddling clothes and attentive care.

target_units.text: She bore her firstborn Son, wrapped Him in swaddling cloths, and laid Him in a manger, because there was no place for them in the lodging place.

relationship: parallel common entrance and departure
rationale: Wisdom declares a common entrance to life and departure; Job likewise connects naked emergence from his mother's womb with naked departure.
source_text: all have one entrance into life, and the same departure.

target_units.text: “I myself came out naked from my mother’s womb, and naked I shall depart there: the Lord gave, and the Lord took away; as it seemed good to the Lord, so it happened: blessed be the name of the Lord.”

relationship: parallel wisdom given in response to prayer
rationale: The speaker receives understanding when he prays; James similarly instructs anyone lacking wisdom to ask God, who gives it.
source_text: Therefore I prayed, and understanding was given me; I called out, and a spirit of wisdom came to me.

target_units.text: But if any of you lacks wisdom, let him ask God, who gives to all generously and without reproach, and it will be given to him.

relationship: parallel wisdom preferred to wealth
rationale: The speaker reckons wealth as nothing beside wisdom; Proverbs likewise values her above gold, silver and costly stones.
source_text: I preferred her to scepters and thrones, and reckoned wealth as nothing in comparison with her.

target_units.text: for trading in her is better than treasures of gold and silver.
She is more valuable than costly stones; nothing evil will stand against her. She is readily known to all who approach her, and nothing precious is worthy of her.

relationship: close precious-metals and stones comparison
rationale: Both explicitly rank wisdom above gold, silver and costly stones, though Wisdom intensifies the comparison through sand and clay.
source_text: Nor did I compare a priceless stone with her, for all gold in her sight is a little sand, and silver will be reckoned as clay before her.

target_units.text: for trading in her is better than treasures of gold and silver.
She is more valuable than costly stones; nothing evil will stand against her. She is readily known to all who approach her, and nothing precious is worthy of her.

relationship: explicit same-chapter explanation of wisdom above light
rationale: Choosing wisdom over light because her radiance never sleeps is explained by her superiority to the sun and the failure of evil to overpower her.
source_text: I loved her more than health and beauty, and chose to have her rather than light, because the radiance that comes from her never sleeps.

target_units.text: For she is more beautiful than the sun and surpasses every arrangement of stars; compared with light, she is found superior.
For night succeeds light, but evil does not overpower wisdom.

relationship: close wealth-in-wisdom's-hand image
rationale: Good things and immeasurable wealth come with wisdom here; Proverbs likewise places wealth and glory in her left hand.
source_text: But all good things came to me together with her, and immeasurable wealth was in her hands.

target_units.text: For length of life and years of living are in her right hand, and wealth and glory in her left.

relationship: internal connection of wisdom and the goods she produces
rationale: Wisdom is called the mother and leader of the accompanying goods; the next chapter similarly describes her as richer than possessions because she works all things.
source_text: I rejoiced in them all, because wisdom leads them, but I did not know that she was their mother.

target_units.text: If wealth is a desirable possession in life, what is richer than wisdom, who works all things?

relationship: parallel wisdom free from deceit and envy
rationale: Learning without deceit and sharing without envy correspond to James's rejection of jealous falsehood and description of heavenly wisdom without hypocrisy.
source_text: I learned without deceit and share without envy; I do not conceal her wealth.

target_units.text: But if you have bitter jealousy and selfish ambition in your heart, do not boast against the truth and lie against it.
This is not the wisdom coming down from above; it is earthly, merely natural, demonic.
For where there are jealousy and selfish ambition, there are disorder and every foul practice.
But the wisdom from above is first pure, then peaceable, considerate, open to persuasion, full of mercy and good fruits, impartial, without hypocrisy.

relationship: related instruction and friendship with God
rationale: Wisdom's disciplined gifts commend people to God's friendship; Jesus likewise connects friendship with obeying His commands and receiving what He heard from the Father.
source_text: For she is an unfailing treasure for human beings; those who acquire it enter into friendship with God, commended by the gifts that come from discipline.

target_units.text: You are My friends if you do what I command you.
I no longer call you slaves, because the slave does not know what his master is doing; but I have called you friends, because I have made known to you everything that I heard from My Father.

relationship: narrative analogue for divinely guided speech
